subject: Hosted API pricing — proposal for tiered slab + one-time onboarding concession
messages:
From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@altosanalytics.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18 10:05 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing — current run rate and ask

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising. Quick follow-up on pricing: we currently consume ~1.6B tokens/month in prod and expect growth to ~3B over the next 6 months (batch + embeddings). Our procurement team asked whether Redwood can map that to a committed per-month token tier with stepped discounts off list (we're evaluating competitive bids).

Two asks: can you share a proposed committed tier schedule and any one-time onboarding or migration credits you can offer for the first quarter? Also need the standard hosted ratecard for legal to review.

I've attached a CSV with our anonymized monthly usage. Procurement is on cc.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Lee
Head of Infrastructure
Altos Analytics

Attachment: Altos_Monthly_Usage.csv (CSV, 48KB)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@altosanalytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18 11:20 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — current run rate and ask

Hi Hannah — great to hear; thanks for the file.

Attached is our Redwood_Standard_Ratecard_v2.pdf for reference. High level thoughts:
- For volumes in the ~1–3B token/month range we typically propose a 3-slab commit (base, growth, overage) with increasing % discounts as tokens scale.
- We can consider a one-time onboarding credit to offset migration FY costs (usually structured as a fixed $ credit against first invoice or token rebate).

Ben (copied) will draft a concrete pricing sketch based on your CSV and propose 1) a per-month commit cadence, 2) per-token prices per slab, and 3) onboarding credit options. Are you open to a 6–12 month minimum? Procurement tends to prefer term commitment for deeper discounts.

Next steps: Ben to propose within 24 hours; if it looks like a custom deviation from our published ratecard we'll route to pricing committee for approval.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Standard_Ratecard_v2.pdf (PDF, 320KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@altosanalytics.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19 09:15 -0700
Subject: Draft pricing sketch for Altos — tiered commit + onboarding concession

Hannah / Priya — attached is a quick workbook with a proposed MAAP (monthly average amp/pack) style commit structure. High level proposal (sketch):

- Term: 12 months minimum (preferred) but we can show a 6-month view for procurement to evaluate.
- Commit tiers (monthly tokens):
  * Tier A: 0 - 500M => list price (no discount)
  * Tier B: 500M - 1.5B => 12% off list
  * Tier C: 1.5B - 3B => 22% off list
  * Tier D: >3B => 28% off list (requires 12mo commit + usage guarantee)
- Overage: billed at blended tiered price or a modest 5% surcharge on published overage rate (open to negotiation).
- Onboarding concession: one-time $60k credit applied to first invoice if a 12-month commit is signed.

Risks / notes: Tier D is a stretch given kernel/capacity economics; we'd need pricing committee signoff for >25% off list. If procurement pushes for deeper discounting in Q1 we can consider a time-limited promo (e.g., first 3 months at additional 5% off).

I've attached 'Proposed_MAAP_Structure.xlsx' with math and sensitivity; please confirm Corp dev/legal pricing path if this needs to become a custom exception.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Proposed_MAAP_Structure.xlsx (Excel, 120KB)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19 14:40 -0700
Subject: FW: Draft pricing sketch for Altos — pricing committee input

Team — forwarding Ben's sketch. Quick internal summary and ask:

- Customer profile: high growth, strategic shooter in analytics; potential to scale regionally (north america + eu).
- Proposed concession: up to 28% off list for Tier D + $60k onboarding credit for a 12-mo commit.
- Recommendation: approve up to 25% off list without Exec pricing committee review; anything >25% should go to pricing committee and Finance. We should also reserve the right to apply a 3-month promotional discount rather than deepen the permanent list discount.

Ask: Marcus — can you run a quick margin impact (NRR/ARR implications) and indicate whether 20–25% is acceptable with the onboarding credit? I can present to pricing committee if we need to escalate. Also flag any redlines we should avoid in the contract (e.g., unlimited data retention SLAs).

Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: FW: Draft pricing sketch for Altos — pricing committee input

Grace / Priya — did the modelling. Short answer: we can support up to a 20% permanent discount across Tier C/D blended if customer signs a 12-month minimum and agrees to a 90% min-commit utilization SLA (protects capacity). Separately we can offer a one-time $60k onboarding credit against month 1 invoice, and a promotional additional 5% off for the first 3 months (time-limited, non-recurring).

Key conditions to include in the quote/contract:
- 12-month minimum term (cancelation triggers catch-up payment for used discounted tokens).
- Minimum utilization threshold (90% of committed average) or blended make-whole payment.
- No open-ended data export SLAs that create additional compute burden (standard export window only).

I will not approve anything greater than 20% without an Exec-level compensation plan; 25%+ requires CCO/CEO signoff. Marcus can present to pricing if Priya needs the >20% path.

Marcus Lin
Director, Finance — Revenue Strategy
Redwood Inference

Hannah — thanks for the patience. Summary of agreed commercial path for procurement to review:

1) Pricing sketch (blended, monthly):
   - Tier B (500M-1.5B): 12% off list
   - Tier C (1.5B-3B): 20% off list (finance-approved)
   - Tier D (>3B): 20% off list with option to revisit at quarter 2 if utilization materially exceeds commit (anything >25% requires Exec approval)
2) Onboarding concession: $60k credit applied to month 1 invoice if a 12-month agreement is executed.
3) Promotion: optional additional 5% credit for first 3 months (non-recurring), subject to final signoff.
4) Terms & protections: 12-month minimum, 90% utilization safeguard, standard data retention/export terms.

Next steps: I will send the formal commercial summary and a DocuSign quote (link below) for procurement. If procurement needs the >25% deeper discount, please notify me and I'll escalate to Exec pricing — that will add time to cycle.
